status_summary: No SBA review ranking its programs by cost-effectiveness and reported to Congress was found. The Administration's FY2026 request proposed about 0.8 billion dollars for SBA, but the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, approved 2026-02-03) provided about 1.3 billion dollars, including 330 million for entrepreneurial development across all 16 programs, according to CRS. CRS reported on 2026-05-27 that the FY2027 request seeks 329.0 million dollars, a 74.7 percent cut, funds entrepreneurial development only for veterans outreach (21.4 million dollars), and raises the Office of Advocacy to 14.1 million dollars; the Administration describes the cut programs as failed counseling and training programs, and CRS cites no ranking or evaluation.

timeline.event: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7148, Public Law 119-75) was approved; per CRS it provides about 1.3 billion dollars for SBA, above the Administration's request of about 0.8 billion dollars, including 330 million for entrepreneurial development.
CRS summarized the FY2027 SBA budget request of 329.0 million dollars, a 74.7 percent decrease from FY2026, which would end funding for most entrepreneurial development programs.

title: Rank SBA programs by cost-effectiveness, hold the budget flat, then end weak programs
